lksg-anwendungsbereich-01.question: How many employees in Germany must a company generally have for the LkSG to apply to it directly?

options.a: At least 500
options.b: At least 1,000
options.c: At least 3,000
options.d: At least 10,000

lksg-anwendungsbereich-01.explanation: Since 1 January 2024, the LkSG applies directly to companies that generally employ at least 1,000 workers in Germany (Sec. 1(1) LkSG). The original threshold of 3,000 employees, in effect from 1 January 2023, was lowered to 1,000 effective 1 January 2024.

lksg-anwendungsbereich-02.question: Which statement about how the LkSG's employee threshold changed over time is correct?

options.a: The threshold was 1,000 employees from the start and was never changed
options.b: From 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023 the threshold was 3,000 employees; since 1 January 2024 it has been 1,000
options.c: The threshold was raised from 1,000 to 3,000 in 2024
options.d: The LkSG only entered into force in 2025 and had no threshold before that

lksg-anwendungsbereich-02.explanation: The LkSG entered into force on 1 January 2023, initially applying to companies with generally at least 3,000 domestic employees; since 1 January 2024 the lowered threshold of at least 1,000 employees applies.

lksg-anwendungsbereich-03.question: Which employees deployed in Germany generally count toward the LkSG threshold under Sec. 1(1) LkSG?

options.a: Only permanent full-time staff; part-time staff do not count
options.b: All domestically employed workers, including group employees posted abroad, and temporary agency workers whose deployment exceeds six months
options.c: Only employees with managerial responsibility
options.d: Only employees who work exclusively abroad

lksg-anwendungsbereich-03.explanation: The count includes all domestically employed workers regardless of working-time scope, group employees posted abroad, and temporary agency workers where their deployment at the hiring company exceeds six months (Sec. 1(1) sentences 2-3 LkSG).

lksg-anwendungsbereich-04.question: How are the domestic employee counts of group subsidiaries treated when calculating whether a parent company crosses the LkSG threshold?

options.a: They are never taken into account
options.b: Only employees of foreign subsidiaries are added
options.c: The domestically employed workers of group companies are attributed to the parent company (Sec. 1(3) LkSG)
options.d: Corporate groups are generally exempt from the LkSG's scope

lksg-anwendungsbereich-04.explanation: Under Sec. 1(3) LkSG, the domestically employed workers of group companies are attributed to the parent company when calculating its employee count - a group-wide view intended to prevent the threshold from being circumvented by spreading staff across several group entities.

lksg-anwendungsbereich-05.question: Which companies fall within the LkSG's territorial scope?

options.a: Only companies with a foreign parent group
options.b: Only publicly listed stock corporations
options.c: Companies with their head office, principal place of business, administrative seat, or registered seat in Germany, and foreign companies with a domestic branch, provided the threshold is met
options.d: Only manufacturing-sector companies

lksg-anwendungsbereich-05.explanation: The LkSG is tied to a domestic business presence: it covers companies with their head office, principal place of business, administrative seat, or registered seat in Germany, as well as foreign companies with a domestic branch, once the relevant employee threshold is reached (Sec. 1(1) LkSG) - regardless of legal form or industry.

lksg-anwendungsbereich-06.question: How does the scope of due diligence duties differ between direct and indirect suppliers?

options.a: There is no difference; both are treated identically
options.b: The full, ongoing due diligence duties apply to the company's own business area and direct suppliers; for indirect suppliers, duties are triggered only on an ad hoc basis once the company has substantiated knowledge of a risk or violation
options.c: Indirect suppliers are subject to stricter duties than direct suppliers
options.d: Due diligence duties apply exclusively to indirect suppliers

lksg-anwendungsbereich-06.explanation: The LkSG scales the depth of control: the full, ongoing due diligence duties apply within the company's own business area and toward direct suppliers. Toward indirect suppliers, they only arise on an ad hoc (event-driven) basis once the company obtains substantiated knowledge of a possible risk or violation (Sec. 9 LkSG).

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-01.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the core due diligence duties listed in Sec. 3(1) LkSG?

options.a: Establishing a risk management system
options.b: Automatically assuming civil liability for all of a supplier's legal violations
options.c: Conducting a risk analysis
options.d: Establishing a grievance mechanism

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-01.explanation: Sec. 3(1) LkSG exhaustively lists the core duties: a risk management system, designating a responsible person/unit, conducting a risk analysis, issuing a policy statement, preventive measures, remedial measures, a grievance mechanism, and documentation/reporting. Automatically assuming civil liability for a supplier's legal violations is explicitly NOT one of them - the LkSG does not create its own strict liability for outcomes (Sec. 3(3) LkSG).

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-02.question: How often must a company conduct a risk analysis under Sec. 5 LkSG at minimum?

options.a: Once when the company is founded, and never again
options.b: Only when explicitly requested by BAFA
options.c: Once a year, plus additionally on an ad hoc basis, e.g. when the risk situation changes materially or the business area expands
options.d: Only once every five years

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-02.explanation: Under Sec. 5(1) and (4) LkSG, the risk analysis must be conducted regularly, at least once a year. It must additionally be repeated on an ad hoc basis, for example when there is a material change or expansion of the risk situation in the company's own business area or at direct suppliers, such as through a new product, project, or business line.

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-03.question: What must an LkSG policy statement under Sec. 6(2) LkSG contain at minimum?

options.a: A description of the process by which the company fulfills its due diligence duties, the prioritized risks identified through the risk analysis, and the human-rights- and environment-related expectations placed on staff and suppliers
options.b: A complete worldwide list of every supplier's name and address
options.c: A guarantee that no risks whatsoever exist anywhere in the supply chain
options.d: Exclusively the company's financial figures

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-03.explanation: The policy statement, which senior management must adopt, must under Sec. 6(2) LkSG describe the process by which the company fulfills its due diligence duties, name the human-rights- and environment-related risks identified and prioritized through the risk analysis, and set out the resulting expectations toward staff and suppliers - not a full supplier address list and not a zero-risk guarantee.

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-04.question: Legally, are the LkSG's due diligence duties an obligation of result (a guarantee that no violation occurs) or an obligation of effort?

options.a: A strict obligation of result - any legal violation occurring anywhere in the supply chain automatically constitutes a breach by the company
options.b: An obligation of effort - the company must take appropriate measures that are actually possible and reasonable for it, but does not guarantee a particular outcome
options.c: Not a legal obligation at all, merely a purely voluntary self-commitment
options.d: An obligation of result, but only for the company's own business area, never toward suppliers

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-04.explanation: Sec. 3(2) LkSG clarifies that the due diligence duties are an obligation of effort: companies must take appropriate measures that are actually possible and reasonable for them to minimize risks and prevent violations, but they do not guarantee a particular outcome. Appropriateness depends among other things on the nature and scope of the business activity, the company's ability to influence the party causing the risk, the severity and reversibility of the expected harm, and the company's own contribution to causing it.

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-05.question: What does Sec. 4(3) LkSG require regarding internal responsibility for monitoring the risk management system?

options.a: Responsibility may never be delegated to a single person
options.b: Only the CEO personally may hold this responsibility
options.c: The company must designate who within the company is responsible for monitoring the risk management system, for example by appointing a human rights officer
options.d: No internal responsibility is legally required

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-05.explanation: Under Sec. 4(3) LkSG, the company must internally designate who is responsible for monitoring the risk management system - in practice this is often done by appointing a human rights officer or comparable role, who reports to senior management regularly, at least once a year.

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-06.question: Which areas does the regular (not just ad hoc) risk analysis under Sec. 5 LkSG primarily cover?

options.a: Exclusively the company's own business area; suppliers are never included
options.b: The company's own business area as well as its direct suppliers
options.c: Exclusively indirect suppliers
options.d: All of the company's end customers

lksg-sorgfaltspflichten-06.explanation: Under Sec. 5 LkSG, the regular risk analysis covers the company's own business area and the conduct of direct suppliers. Indirect suppliers - as with preventive and remedial measures - are generally only included on an ad hoc basis, once the company has substantiated knowledge of a possible risk or violation (Sec. 9 LkSG).

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-01.question: Which measure is a typical preventive measure within the company's own business area under Sec. 6(3) LkSG?

options.a: Completely halting all sourcing from countries considered risky
options.b: Implementing the policy statement within the company's own business area, appropriate procurement practices, and training for relevant staff
options.c: Exclusively publishing an annual business report
options.d: Abandoning all internal control mechanisms

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-01.explanation: Sec. 6(3) LkSG names, among others, embedding the policy statement, factoring human-rights- and environment-related expectations into purchasing decisions (procurement practices), and training staff in relevant business areas as typical preventive measures within the company's own business area. A blanket withdrawal from entire countries is specifically not the statute's preferred approach - the LkSG favors exerting influence over simply withdrawing.

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-02.question: Which preventive measure toward direct suppliers does Sec. 6(4) LkSG specifically envisage?

options.a: Factoring human-rights- and environment-related expectations into supplier selection, contractual assurances, training offers, and risk-based control measures
options.b: Fully taking over every supplier's operations directly
options.c: A duty to personally visit every supplier on-site every year, regardless of risk
options.d: Automatically excluding every supplier located in a non-EU country

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-02.explanation: Toward direct suppliers, Sec. 6(4) LkSG names, among others, factoring human-rights- and environment-related concerns into supplier selection, contractual assurances (e.g. codes of conduct), training and capacity-building offers, and risk-based control measures - the concrete design of which depends on case-by-case appropriateness, not a rigid annual on-site-visit rule.

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-03.question: What must a company do if a violation of a protected legal position has already occurred within its own business area (not at a supplier)?

options.a: The company can freely decide whether and when to respond
options.b: It must immediately take appropriate measures to end the violation - within its own business area this generally means ending it right away
options.c: It is enough to mention the violation in the next annual report
options.d: A response is only required for violations that become public through the press

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-03.explanation: Sec. 7(1) LkSG obliges the company to immediately take appropriate remedial measures once a violation has already occurred within its own business area. Because the company has direct control there, this regularly means the violation must be ended without delay - a stricter expectation than toward suppliers, where the company often only has indirect influence.

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-04.question: For a violation that has already occurred at a direct supplier, what is the statutorily required first step before terminating the business relationship?

options.a: Immediate, unconditional termination of the business relationship with no further steps
options.b: Ignoring the violation as long as the supplier is economically important
options.c: Developing and implementing a concept to end or minimize the violation, with a concrete timeline; terminating the relationship is only a last resort in particularly severe cases with no prospect of improvement
options.d: Simply reporting it to BAFA, without the company itself having to act

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-04.explanation: Under Sec. 7(2) LkSG, when a violation occurs at a direct supplier, the company must first promptly develop and implement a concept to end or minimize it, including a concrete timeline. Terminating the business relationship is provided for by law only as a last resort, applicable where the violation is particularly severe, remedial measures show no prospect of improvement after exhausting means of influence, and expanding that influence is not reasonably feasible.

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-05.question: Under what condition must a company take preventive or remedial measures toward indirect suppliers as well?

options.a: Never - indirect suppliers are completely exempt from the LkSG
options.b: Always and regardless of any knowledge, to the same extent as for direct suppliers
options.c: When the company obtains substantiated knowledge of a possible violation of a protected legal position or an environment-related duty at an indirect supplier (Sec. 9 LkSG)
options.d: Only if a competitor publicly calls on the company to do so

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-05.explanation: Sec. 9 LkSG provides for ad hoc duties toward indirect suppliers: once the company obtains substantiated knowledge - for example through a complaint under Sec. 8 LkSG or its own reports - of a possible violation, it must promptly conduct a risk analysis and take appropriate preventive and remedial measures, taking into account its actual ability to exert influence.

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-06.question: How often must a company review the effectiveness of its preventive measures at minimum?

options.a: Never - once introduced, measures are permanently deemed sufficient
options.b: Once a year, plus on an ad hoc basis, e.g. when the risk situation changes materially
options.c: Only upon a court order
options.d: Only when first entering a new country's market

lksg-praevention_abhilfe-06.explanation: Under Sec. 6(5) LkSG, the effectiveness of preventive measures must be reviewed once a year and additionally on an ad hoc basis, for example when the risk situation in the company's own business area or at direct suppliers changes or expands materially - measures must be updated as needed rather than introduced once and never revisited.

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-01.question: What purpose does the grievance mechanism under Sec. 8 LkSG serve?

options.a: It exclusively serves internal assessment of the company's own workforce salary matters
options.b: It enables individuals to flag human-rights- and environment-related risks and violations arising within the company's own business area or in the supply chain
options.c: It fully replaces state courts
options.d: It exclusively handles customer complaints about product quality

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-01.explanation: The grievance mechanism under Sec. 8 LkSG is meant to enable individuals to flag human-rights- and environment-related risks, and violations of human-rights- or environment-related duties, arising within the company's own business area or at a supplier. It is an early-warning and reporting tool, not a substitute for courts or a pure customer-service channel.

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-02.question: Who is entitled to use the grievance mechanism under Sec. 8 LkSG?

options.a: Exclusively the company's own permanent employees
options.b: Exclusively state supervisory authorities
options.c: Persons personally affected by a risk or violation, as well as persons who have otherwise gained knowledge of it - such as NGOs or trade unions
options.d: Exclusively the company's shareholders

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-02.explanation: Sec. 8(1) LkSG deliberately grants broad access: both persons directly affected and persons who have otherwise gained knowledge of a possible violation are entitled to use it - this includes, for example, employees of suppliers, NGOs, or trade unions, not just the company's own staff.

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-03.question: What requirements does Sec. 8 LkSG impose on how the grievance mechanism is set up?

options.a: It must be reachable exclusively by phone; other channels are impermissible
options.b: Among other things, there must be a publicly available rules of procedure, confidentiality must be maintained, whistleblowers must be protected from retaliation for raising a complaint, and the procedure must ensure access, transparency, and impartiality
options.c: Rules of procedure are expressly prohibited by law
options.d: Complainants must always identify themselves with their full name and address

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-03.explanation: Sec. 8(3) and (4) LkSG require, among other things, publicly available rules of procedure setting out access and the criteria for handling reports, confidentiality of identity, protection of whistleblowers from disadvantage or punishment for raising the complaint, and an impartial, transparent procedure accessible to everyone potentially affected.

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-04.question: Must every obligated company necessarily build a completely new, purely internal grievance mechanism of its own?

options.a: No, under Sec. 8(5) LkSG the company may instead participate in an external or industry-wide (multi-stakeholder) grievance mechanism, provided it meets the statutory requirements to an equivalent standard
options.b: Yes, participating in external mechanisms is impermissible under all circumstances
options.c: No, a grievance mechanism is entirely optional for every company
options.d: Yes, but only for companies with fewer than 1,000 employees

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-04.explanation: Sec. 8(5) LkSG expressly allows companies to participate in an external grievance mechanism instead of running their own, for example an industry-wide or multi-stakeholder mechanism, as long as it meets the statutory requirements for accessibility, transparency, impartiality, and whistleblower protection to an equivalent standard.

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-05.question: What role does the grievance mechanism typically play in a company obtaining 'substantiated knowledge' of a risk at an indirect supplier?

options.a: The grievance mechanism has no legal connection to this at all
options.b: Substantiated knowledge can only arise from an official government notice, never from a complaint
options.c: A sufficiently concrete report received through the grievance mechanism is a typical trigger for substantiated knowledge, which can then trigger ad hoc duties toward indirect suppliers under Sec. 9 LkSG
options.d: Complaints about indirect suppliers are legally impermissible

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-05.explanation: A concrete, plausible report received through the grievance mechanism is one of the typical ways a company gains substantiated knowledge within the meaning of Sec. 9(1) LkSG - thereby triggering the ad hoc duty to conduct a risk analysis and consider appropriate preventive or remedial measures, including toward an indirect supplier.

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-06.question: How does the LkSG grievance mechanism under Sec. 8 LkSG relate to the internal reporting channel under the Whistleblower Protection Act (HinSchG)?

options.a: The two mechanisms are legally identical and must by law be merged into a single channel
options.b: They are two mechanisms with different scopes (supply-chain human rights/environment under the LkSG, a much broader range of legal violations under the HinSchG); companies may combine them organizationally, but are not required to
options.c: The HinSchG fully abolishes the LkSG grievance mechanism
options.d: An LkSG grievance mechanism is only permissible if no HinSchG reporting channel already exists

lksg-beschwerdeverfahren-06.explanation: The LkSG grievance mechanism and the HinSchG internal reporting channel serve different statutory purposes: the LkSG mechanism focuses on human-rights- and environment-related risks/violations in the company's own business area and supply chain, while the HinSchG covers a much broader range of legal violations. Many companies combine both channels organizationally for efficiency, but there is no legal requirement to do so.

lksg-sanktionen-01.question: Which authority is responsible for the state supervision and enforcement of the LkSG?

options.a: The Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin)
options.b: The Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control (BAFA)
options.c: The Federal Cartel Office (Bundeskartellamt)
options.d: The Federal Court of Justice (BGH)

lksg-sanktionen-01.explanation: The competent supervisory authority under Sec. 19 LkSG is the Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control (BAFA). It reviews compliance with due diligence duties, can request reports, issue administrative orders, and initiate fine proceedings - distinct from BaFin, which is responsible for financial supervision (e.g. anti-money-laundering).

lksg-sanktionen-02.question: Up to what amount can a fine under Sec. 24 LkSG generally be imposed for particularly serious violations - such as failing to implement preventive or remedial measures, or failing to establish a grievance mechanism?

options.d: Up to €8 million as a fixed amount unrelated to turnover

lksg-sanktionen-02.explanation: Sec. 24 LkSG tiers the fine ranges by severity of the violation. For the most serious violations - such as failing to implement preventive or remedial measures, lacking a remediation concept, or not establishing a grievance mechanism - the statute provides for a fine of up to €800,000. Less serious organizational duties (e.g. risk analysis) carry a maximum of €500,000, and purely documentation/reporting duties a maximum of €100,000.

lksg-sanktionen-03.question: What additional, turnover-based fine rule applies to companies with an average annual turnover above €400 million?

options.a: For certain serious violations, a fine of up to 2% of the average worldwide group annual turnover over the last three financial years can be imposed
options.b: Fines are eliminated entirely for such companies
options.c: The fine ceiling is capped at a flat €1,000 for such companies
options.d: A fixed amount of exactly €400 million applies as the fine

lksg-sanktionen-03.explanation: For companies with an average annual turnover above €400 million, Sec. 24(3)-(4) LkSG provides that, for certain particularly serious violations, the fine can be up to 2% of the average worldwide group annual turnover over the last three financial years - a rule designed to make the fixed €800,000 ceiling more effective for very large companies by scaling it to turnover.

lksg-sanktionen-04.question: What additional consequence can a company face for a substantial fine under the LkSG, beyond the fine itself?

options.a: Forced sale of the company to a competitor
options.b: Temporary exclusion from public procurement (Sec. 22 LkSG), provided the fine decision exceeds a certain threshold
options.c: Automatic revocation of the business license for all business lines
options.d: An immediate criminal prison sentence for management without any further proceedings

lksg-sanktionen-04.explanation: Sec. 22 LkSG provides that a company can be temporarily excluded - for up to three years - from public procurement once a fine above a certain amount has been imposed. The company can end this exclusion early by demonstrating successful self-cleaning (a concept comparable to procurement law's self-cleaning rules, e.g. Sec. 125 GWB).

lksg-sanktionen-05.question: Does a violation of the LkSG's due diligence duties create a standalone civil liability of the company toward third parties (e.g. affected persons abroad)?

options.a: Yes, every LkSG violation automatically creates its own damages claim under the LkSG
options.b: No - Sec. 3(3) sentence 1 LkSG clarifies that a violation of duties under this Act does not create standalone civil liability; liability claims arising from other legal provisions remain unaffected, as does the special standing to sue under Sec. 11 LkSG
options.c: Yes, but only if the company also has a turnover above €400 million
options.d: This question is not addressed in the LkSG and is therefore entirely open

lksg-sanktionen-05.explanation: Sec. 3(3) sentence 1 LkSG expressly clarifies that a breach of duties under this Act does not create standalone civil liability. Liability claims arising independently of the LkSG under other legal provisions remain unaffected. In addition, Sec. 11 LkSG allows domestic trade unions and certain NGOs, authorized by the affected persons, to assert those persons' rights before German courts on their behalf (a form of special standing to sue).

lksg-sanktionen-06.question: As of summer 2026, what is the status of a bill that would abolish the reporting duty under Sec. 10 LkSG and narrow the fine catalogue to a few particularly severe violations?

options.a: The bill has already been law since 2023 and has fully eliminated the reporting duty
options.b: The federal cabinet approved a corresponding government bill in September 2025; as of early 2026 it was still in parliamentary proceedings and had not yet entered into force as of this module's writing
options.c: No such bill exists and it has never been discussed
options.d: The bill has already been finally rejected by the Bundestag

lksg-sanktionen-06.explanation: In September 2025, the federal cabinet approved a government bill that would remove the reporting duty under Sec. 10 LkSG and narrow future fines to a handful of particularly serious violations (e.g. failing to implement preventive/remedial measures, lacking a grievance mechanism), framed as temporary relief pending implementation of the EU's CSDDD supply-chain directive. The bill was debated in the Bundestag in early 2026 and referred to committee, but had not yet been passed - the current legal position described in this module (including the reporting duty and the full fine catalogue) remained unchanged as of this module's writing. Always verify the current state of the law before production/commercial use.
